headline: Brazil Cuts Workweek to 40 Hours, Ending Era of 6-Day Labor
meta_description: Brazil's Senate votes overwhelmingly to reduce the standard workweek from 44 to 40 hours, granting full-time workers two paid days off for the first time since…
summary_short: Brazil's Senate votes 75-to-1 to cut the workweek from 44 to 40 hours, marking the first labor reform in 35 years and giving millions of workers an extra day of rest.
body:
For millions of Brazilians who wake early, board crowded buses, and work their shift before heading home, life is about to change in a meaningful way. Brazil's Senate voted 75 to 1 in favor of Constitutional Amendment 221, reducing the standard workweek from 44 hours to 40 hours and guaranteeing two paid days off for full-time employees. The shift represents the first legislative change to labor hours since 1988, when the workweek was reduced from 48 hours to 44. As Senate President Davi Alcolumbre noted, "One more day of rest means more time for family."

The amendment was supported by both the incumbent president and his political opponent, who voted in favor online just 11 days before the second-round elections. This rare bipartisan backing ensured swift passage through both chambers of Congress without requiring executive signature. The reduction phases in over time: 42 hours beginning 60 days after passage, then dropping to the full 40 hours a year later—giving employers time to reorganize schedules or hire additional workers.

Brazil, once among the world's richest nations still requiring a 6-day workweek, now aligns with international labor standards. The specific days off will be negotiated between unions and employers, though most workers are expected to secure either Saturday or Sunday. Originally introduced in 2019 as a proposal to shrink the workweek to 34 hours, the amendment was adjusted to 40 hours—still a significant victory for Brazil's workers seeking better work-life balance.
quick_facts: Brazil's Senate voted 75-to-1 for the amendment
Workweek reduces from 44 to 40 hours over one year
Two paid days off now guaranteed for full-time workers
Both presidential candidates supported the measure
